subject: English
passage: As historian Ashok Wijaya notes, eponymous doctrines misattributed to later popularizers ______ there is the Monroe Doctrine; in economics, the Laffer curve; and in political theory, the Machiavellian principle. Each of these bears the name of a figure who was not, in fact, its originator.
prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. The colon after 'abound' follows a complete independent clause and properly introduces the complex series of exemplars that follows. Because the items in the series contain internal commas (each pairs a field, such as 'in diplomacy,' with a named concept, such as 'the Monroe Doctrine'), semicolons are used to separate the items. The comma after 'diplomacy' correctly offsets the prepositional phrase from the rest of the first item.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. A comma after 'abound' cannot introduce the complex series that follows; a colon is required to signal that a list elaborating the main clause is coming. The comma also misleadingly absorbs 'in diplomacy' into the main clause rather than marking it as the opening of the first series item.
